catalog_quote: [Jones 1988: 327] Word-stress normally falls on the penultimate or antepenultimate syllable. Stress on final syllables is generally avoided in Sardinian. Indeed, a final epenthetic vowel is added to Latin monosyllables to yield paroxytonic forms. ... However, oxytonic forms do arise, mainly in Campidanese and Logudorese, as a result of elision of an intervocalic consonant: Log. /'pe/ (< pedem) 'foot', Camp. /dro'mi/ (< dOrmIre) 'to sleep'. ... if two or more clitics are added, the stress may (optionally) be shifted to the penultimate syllable of the whole sequence: /'narami/ 'tell me', /'naramilu/, /nara'milu/ 'tell me it'. [Mereu 2020: 402] Drawing on Porru's dictionary (Porru 1832), Bolognesi (1998) reports that 85% of underived words show stress in the penultimate syllable, e.g. pratza [ˈprattsa] 'town square', traballu [traˈbːallu] 'work, job', ventana [vɛnˈtana] 'window'. sweep_summary: One works with stress in the title, Roca 1999 'Stress in the Romance languages' (Eurotyp 4, pp. 659-812): a comparative Romance chapter whose Sardinian data come from the Campidanese dialect area (p. 663, Bolognesi p.c.). Full text is paywalled at De Gruyter (no repository copy found; Semantic Scholar's OA link is a mis-link; 662, 663, 666, 667, 670, 702: p. 666 states that Sardinian, 'Campidanese in particular, strongly disfavour[s] final stress', the only native Campidanese oxytone being meri 'afternoon/evening', with final-stressed monosyllables (di, mi, ti, si) repaired; p. 667 says Logudorese is more liberal (caffe) but still disfavours oxytones. This refines the catalog's Jones 1988 quote (penult/antepenult stress, final stress avoided, some oxytones from elision) and is consistent with the 'lexical' coding; it does not supersede Jones. The already-on-disk 2009 Campidanese orthographic norm (Arregulas, rule h) confirms paroxytone as the unmarked default with marked oxytones and proparoxytones. Priority high for obtaining the full Roca chapter (pp. 662-671, esp. 666-667 and 671, which the index lists for Campidanese but which no snippet reached). Records and logged in there.

new_statements.reading: Roca (using Campidanese-area data, with Bolognesi as consultant) says Campidanese essentially bans final stress: one native oxytone (meri), and final-stressed monosyllables are repaired; stress therefore lies on the penult or antepenult. This is snippet-level evidence (full chapter paywalled); it refines rather than replaces the catalog's Jones 1988 statement, which additionally allows oxytones from intervocalic-consonant elision (a point Roca's visible snippets do not address). Catalog classification lexical (penult/antepenult, not predictable) is not contradicted.

This is a difference in the count of final-stress exceptions, not in the classification: both sources say final stress is banned/avoided and repaired,…

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote check passes for both cited loci in copies we hold (Jones 1988: 327 scanned text; Mereu 2020: 402 publisher PDF). The classification lexical (penult-dominant, lexical antepenult class, final stress avoided/repaired, distinctive minimal pairs, right-edge window) is exactly what Jones and Mereu say, and the open Torres-Tamarit et al. 2017 paper downloaded now independently confirms the final-stress prohibition and epenthesis repair. The sources are competent and modern but second-tier for stress: a handbook sketch plus a JIPA Illustration that relays Bolognesi 1998. The one live issue is the recorded contradiction with StressTyp2's weight-sensitive U/P code (via Roca 1999): neither held source mentions weight, but neither denies the standard Romance restriction that a closed penult excludes antepenult stress, which Bolognesi 1998 or Roca 1999 would state or refute. Hence 'adequate' rather than 'well-so

States that Sardinian, Campidanese in particular, strongly disfavours final stress: the only native Campidanese oxytone is meri 'afternoon/evening'; final-stressed monosyllables (di, mi, ti, si..) get an epenthetic/paragogic extension; Logudorese tolerates a few more oxytones (caffe) but still disfavours them; final stress in Nuorese survives in toponyms and, per Pittau 1972, only two common-noun exceptions. sources.quote: 'de scriri s'acentu tònicu apitzus de fueddu ossìtonu o truncu (acentau in s'ùrtimu sìllaba: [issu] pa-pàt, nara-mì) e proparossìtonu o lìscinu (acentau in sa de tres ùrtimus sìllabas: àr-vi-u, là-ca-na) e no apitzus de fueddu parossìtonu o pranu (acentau in sa de duas ùrtimus sìllabas: is-su pa-pat, par-ti-u)' [= write the stress accent on oxytones and proparoxytones, not on paroxytones]; sec. 16.2: 'is particìpius de sa de 2 depint tenni sèmpiri s'acentu scritu in sa de tres ùrtimus sìllabas' [2nd-conjugation participles always carry the written accent on the antepenult; /-iu/ unstressed in conj. 2, stressed in conj. 3].
sources.locator: orthography rule h) (bilingual Sardinian/Italian, PDF text p. 69-70); sec. 16.2 on participles
sources.note: Normative orthography for standard Campidanese: paroxytone stress is the unmarked default (no written accent); oxytones (papàt, naramì) and proparoxytones (àrviu, làcana) exist and must be marked; conjugation-conditioned contrast in participle stress (conj. 2 antepenult vs conj. 3 penult). Consistent with a lexically contrastive penult/antepenult (plus minority final) system; it is a spelling rule, not a descriptive stress statement.
